title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 14
paragraphs: These, then, were perishing around the Hollows of Euboea. Meanwhile the barbarians at Aphetai, when day had dawned on them — a welcome sight — were keeping their ships quiet and were content, in their wretched plight, to remain still for the present. But to the Greeks there came a reinforcement of fifty-three Athenian ships. Their arrival gave the Greeks greater courage, and they were further heartened by a report that those of the barbarians who had been sailing around Euboea had all been destroyed by the storm. So they waited for the same hour of the day as before, and then sailed out and fell upon some Cilician ships; and having destroyed these, they sailed back when darkness came on and returned to Artemisium.
